Arctic char FTZF1 forms are expressed during embryogenesis, and in steroidogenic and lipid metabolising tissues during adult life.
two forms of the NR5A gene family are expressed in the Arctic char during development and in adult tissues, with the highest levels of expression in tissues involved in steroid synthesis.

the expression pattern of FTZ-F1 genes in Arctic char and how they are involved in cholesterol metabolism and steroidogenesis.
the expression and distribution patterns of two FTZ-F1 genes in Arctic char during different life stages.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NR5A1 and NR5A2 groups are not as clearly separated in teleosts as in other vertebrates, and that NR5A genes may have been recruited for new functions during evolution of the vertebrate lineage.

the two Arctic char NR5A2 forms are involved in steroidogenesis, as well as cholesterol transfer and metabolism, and that these genes are important in early development and throughout the lifetime of teleosts.
